nodes.name: Sandbox User
nodes.description: Human or orchestrating agent who logs in at the IdP and asks mediatore for a sandbox. Never talks to Kubernetes, SPIRE or the hypervisor directly; the broker is the only front door for delegated sandboxes.

nodes.name: Identity Provider (Dex, Google, Auth0, Entra ID)
nodes.description: Upstream OIDC issuer, any the configuration names (ADR-0017): Dex bridging GitHub or LDAP, Google, Auth0, all on the session path (a public PKCE client, the refresh grant before every issue, ADR-0013); Entra ID also performs the On-Behalf-Of exchange (ADR-0016): the caller's access token for mediatore is exchanged at claim creation for a refresh token issued to mediatore for that user, and every token issue is a refresh_token grant naming the audience's resource. mediatore's own STS stands in for delegation on issuers without one (ADR-0003).

nodes.name: mediatore
nodes.description: The identity broker: one binary, two listeners (user-facing bearer HTTPS behind the ingress, sandbox-facing SPIFFE mTLS terminated in-process on aws-lc-rs), a claim watcher and a token backend per audience (ADR-0002, ADR-0003, ADR-0007). Runs as a restricted, non-root Deployment in banlieue-system; its SVID lives only in process memory.

nodes.name: User API (bearer)
nodes.description: POST/GET/DELETE /v1/claims. Validates the caller's IdP token (issuer, audience, signature via JWKS, group gate: one of required_group, required_groups or an explicit allow_any_authenticated, ADR-0046) and creates an AgentSandbox with spec.subject taken from the validated token (ADR-0008). The namespace is decided here, at TB-1 (ADR-0046): with sandboxes.namespaces set (a namespace-to-groups map in the broker's configuration, not a node), the request must name a namespace and the caller's token groups must intersect that namespace's groups, else 403 (one body for an unlisted and an unqualified namespace); an omitted namespace is 400 namespace_required; without the map it is the single sandboxes.namespace as before. GET and DELETE take ?namespace= and apply the same group check plus the owner check (a namespace outside the map or not the caller's is 404). ADR-0053: an audience scoped to namespaces (audiences[].namespaces, each entry that namespace's rules, the audience's own rules the ceiling every entry must sit inside) is refused to a namespace it does not list as 400 unknown_audience, the same answer as an audience that does not exist, and a claim's routes, the gateway's routes and every mint read the claim record's own namespace. Phase 2 (policy.audiences: shadow by default, enforce): the claim must name a policy that resolves to a verified, unexpired bundle (400 policy_required, 400 unknown_policy, 503 policy_not_synced until every watched namespace was listed), the bundle must grant each audience (400 unknown_audience) and its lease cover ttl_seconds (400 ttl_exceeds_policy), and a claim's rules, endpoints and credential lifetime are the bundle's grant bounded by the audience's own rules (the ceiling), read from the claim's current bundle at every ask, so a missing, expired or unverified bundle takes the audiences away. GET answers from the resource's status, DELETE deletes it and the finalizer does the rest. Under dev_mode the in-memory store and dev binder stand in. crates/mediatore-api + mediatore-entra. Since ADR-0045 also GET /v1/claims/{name}/logs (NDJSON, follow, since, tail): the stored output of the caller's own claim, the same subject and namespace checks, 501 unless logs.enabled, one audit line per read and never the content; and POST /v1/claims refuses workload.logs: true with 501 when logs are off.

nodes.name: Sandbox API (SPIFFE mTLS)
nodes.description: POST /v1/nodes, GET /v1/me, POST /v1/me/report, POST /v1/me/exit (ADR-0033: the workload's exit recorded, the claim released as a delete releases it), POST /v1/token over SPIFFE mTLS: client certificate required, chain verified against the trust-domain bundle, peer SPIFFE ID taken from the verified URI SAN and restricted to /banlieue/node/*, /banlieue/claim/* and, since ADR-0053, the gateway authorizer's identity spiffe://<td>/gateway/authorizer (Naming::is_gateway_authorizer), which the gateway routes alone accept; the gateway listeners' identity spiffe://<td>/gateway, admitted from ADR-0028 until then, no longer completes a handshake, other than while the transition switch accept_plain_gateway_identity is on. A connection ends at its peer certificate's notAfter. Node identities may register and fetch their subject, claim identities may request audience-scoped tokens (minted by the STS or Entra, or since ADR-0032 the operator's own credential for an audience via: secret, handed with the header it goes in). The dev header exists only under dev_mode on a loopback listener (ADR-0007). crates/mediatore-api. GET /v1/me also carries the operator's pull credential for the registry the claim's image names, and no other (ADR-0022). ADR-0040: POST /v1/gateway/claims/{uid}/credential, accepted only from the gateway authorizer's identity (ADR-0053), returns an audience's credential for the gateway to place when the audience is inject: gateway; POST /v1/token refuses such an audience with 403 placed_at_gateway; GET /v1/gateway/claims/{uid} carries the gateway-placed routes (endpoint, rules, header names, non-secret extra headers) and GET /v1/me carries credential: gateway and the inject port on those routes. Since ADR-0045 also POST /v1/me/logs: the claim's node ships the redacted workload output, accepted only for a claim that opted in, shape- and size-checked, rate-limited to two batches a second, idempotent on the sequence number, a follower of the claim woken once the batch is stored, 501 unless logs.enabled.

nodes.name: Claim Watcher and AgentSandbox Reconciler
nodes.description: Reconciles AgentSandbox (ADR-0008, built): creates and owns one VirtualMachineClaim per sandbox, named after it, at most once; writes the store record keyed by the claim's UID; mirrors the claim's status plus whether the entry is set (Ready only when Bound and set); refuses, before any claim exists, a sandbox naming an audience or issuer outside mediatore's configuration; holds a finalizer that releases the record, deletes the claim and lets the object go only once the claim is gone. Watches VirtualMachineClaim (managed-by label) and VirtualMachine (pool members): on Bound resolves the node by the EK hash the claim mirrors (never by name, address or UUID), binds through the Reconciler, fails an unresolved bind after a bounded wait by deleting the claim, releases on Releasing / Failed / deletion and at resync; declares a node entry when a member publishes its vTPM endorsement certificate; one replica leads by Lease (ADR-0011, built). Under ADR-0026 (implemented) the same loop reflects notaio's bundle ConfigMaps in the configured namespaces, verifies each against the configured keys, moves the policy's version floor in the store by a compare and set, caches the verified payload, and on each reconcile of a sandbox, and whenever its policy's bundle changes, reports every way the broker would allow more than the bundle (codes P001 to P012) as a log line and the PolicyConformant condition; in shadow it admits, binds and mints exactly as before; under policy.egress: enforce the bundle's servable direct egress is added to the claim's routes at the gateway (ADR-0030), and a gateway-placed audience must be one the claim's policy admits (ADR-0040). Since ADR-0054 a sandbox's policyRef is resolved only in the namespaces its own namespace draws from (policy.sources in the broker's configuration, a mapping from sandbox namespace to policy namespaces; by default the sandbox's own namespace alone, never a fallback across policy.namespaces): a name in no source is P011, a name held by two sources is P012, and both read the same for a policy elsewhere and a policy nowhere; under enforce such a sandbox is Failed with policy_not_resolved before any claim exists and a sandbox whose sources are not yet read is held, while in shadow it is created and reported. Never holds a SPIRE admin identity (ADR-0006). crates/mediatore-claims.

nodes.name: STS
nodes.description: Self-issued ES256 tokens with an RFC 8693 act claim naming the claim SVID as actor; JWKS derived from the signing key and served at /.well-known/jwks.json. Used for audiences whose backend is `sts` (ADR-0003). crates/mediatore-sts.

nodes.name: AgentSandbox resources
nodes.description: Namespaced CRD mediatore.io/v1beta1 (v1alpha1 until ADR-0048, 2026-11-18; v1alpha1 served beside it as the same object, deprecated, conversion None, ADR-0049), served and reconciled by mediatore (ADR-0008, built: roadmap 08; created through the broker only in a namespace of sandboxes.namespaces that the caller's groups admit, ADR-0046; schema generated from the Rust type into deploy/base/crds). The request for one sandbox: subject, poolRef or poolSelector (exactly one, by CEL; poolSelector: {} is every pool in the namespace, an omitted field never is; the pool bound from is mirrored into status.poolRef, ADR-0044), selection (optional; strategy LongestReady, MostAvailable or Spread, how banlieue ranks the Ready members of the matched pools; absent is LongestReady and mediatore writes no default; copied to the claim verbatim, ADR-0047), ttlSeconds, audiences, workload. Created by the user API on POST /v1/claims or declaratively by anything with RBAC on agentsandboxes; spec.subject is pinned to the caller by the mediatore-agentsandbox-subject admission policy unless the caller is mediatore's ServiceAccount or a listed broker, and the whole spec is immutable afterwards. Never carries a credential. Owns exactly one VirtualMachineClaim; a finalizer holds it until the claim and its ClusterStaticEntry are gone. Status mirrors the claim plus whether the entry is set. ADR-0026 (implemented) adds spec.policyRef, the name of a SandboxPolicy in the sandbox's namespace, optional and immutable with the rest of the spec; naming a policy grants nothing in shadow, and under policy.egress: enforce it is what admits the bundle's direct egress (ADR-0030). ADR-0045 adds spec.workload.logs, the requester's opt-in to output capture (boolean, default false, immutable with the rest of the spec).

nodes.name: Claim Store (the Kubernetes API)
nodes.description: What the broker remembers, in the Kubernetes API (ADR-0034, superseding the database of ADR-0012): the claim record on the AgentSandbox status (status.record, the store's alone: the SPIRE entry id, the node, the bind deadline, the revocation, the policy incarnation and bundle version, the guest's report, the workload's exit; the claim UID and the node as labels), the sealed refresh envelope in a Secret owned by the sandbox (key id, nonce, AES-256-GCM ciphertext bound to the sandbox UID; parked by the API, claimed by the reconciler, rotated at every mint, emptied on revocation), attested nodes as SandboxNode resources (EK hash, agent SPIFFE ID, DMI UUID, banned), removed by the watcher once no VM publishes their EK hash (ADR-0039), notaio's version floors as PolicyFloor resources moved by compare-and-set on resourceVersion. Since ADR-0057 an update of a claim's record is conditional on the resourceVersion it was read at, a release carries no precondition, the status is written before the Secrets, and the record names its sandbox (sandboxUid, namespace). An ended claim is held by its finalizer for store.retention_secs and then swept, the audit line in the log. In memory under dev_mode only. ADR-0043 decision 4: the sealed envelope in a claim's Secret is deleted, not blanked, when the claim is released, and an envelope for a claim that never binds is deleted when the claim's ttl_seconds has passed counted from creation; the released-claim marker moves to the AgentSandbox status record. ADR-0045 adds the workload output ring beside the session Secrets (data-asset-workload-output).

nodes.name: OpenBao (transit, PKI)
nodes.description: Encryption as a service for the refresh envelopes (ADR-0015): the transit engine holds the derived sealing key, encrypts and decrypts on request with the binding UID as context, authorises every call by a token it issued to the broker's ServiceAccount (Kubernetes auth, audience openbao) and rotates the key in place. Since ADR-0016 the same engine may hold the RSA key that signs the broker's client assertion for Entra (transit sign, PSS), so the credential that lets mediatore act as itself at Entra never enters the process. Since ADR-0031 its PKI engine is also the SPIRE server's upstream authority: a ten-year root on a dedicated mount signs the server's intermediate CA every ca_ttl (root/sign-intermediate, the one path the server's role may call), so the trust bundle every pool VM and gateway starts from is that root and outlives the server's CA. Reached over TLS the broker and the server verify against a configured CA. In kind: make kind-openbao.

nodes.name: STS Signing Key
nodes.description: EC P-256 private key the STS signs with. A PEM file (sts.signing_key_file, the one shape StsConfig takes); a signer over OpenBao transit is planned, not built. Whoever holds it can mint tokens for any configured audience: guarded asset (threat model TB-1).

nodes.name: Sealing Key
nodes.description: The key that wraps refresh material before it reaches the store (ADR-0012 decision 3). Work shape (ADR-0015): a derived transit key inside OpenBao that never leaves it; the broker holds only a short-lived OpenBao token obtained with its projected ServiceAccount token, and the binding UID is the derivation context. Homelab shape: a 32-byte key from a Secret volume, read into broker memory at start (local sealer).

nodes.name: Kubernetes API Server
nodes.description: Management-cluster API server. mediatore creates and watches AgentSandbox and VirtualMachineClaim through it, and declares SPIRE registration entries as ClusterStaticEntry resources through it. The mediatore-agentsandbox-subject VAP pins spec.subject to the caller except for mediatore's ServiceAccount and listed brokers (ADR-0008); banlieue's claim-subject VAP does the same for claims, with mediatore's ServiceAccount as a listed broker; the mediatore-clusterstaticentry VAP restricts the broker's ServiceAccount to the two entry shapes under /banlieue/ (ADR-0006).

nodes.name: banlieue Control Plane
nodes.description: Schedules pool members and binds VirtualMachineClaims to Ready VMs. mediatore consumes its CRDs (banlieue-api types) and never bypasses it; the Kubernetes API is the only interface between the two (banlieue non-negotiable #1, mediatore ADR-0002).

nodes.name: notaio Policy Control Plane
nodes.description: Reviews SandboxPolicy resources and compiles each into a signed bundle: a DSSE envelope over the effective policy (per audience its access, scopes, ttlSeconds, endpoints and rules in the broker's own rule shape; direct egress; the lease's maxDurationSeconds; the policy's namespace, name and uid; a version that only goes up; a notAfter), signed by a key in OpenBao transit that notaio alone can use, published in the policy's namespace as the ConfigMap <policy>-bundle (key bundle.dsse.json, label app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=notaio). mediatore reads what it publishes through the Kubernetes API and nothing else; the signing key never leaves notaio's transit (ADR-0026).

nodes.name: SandboxPolicy bundles (ConfigMaps)
nodes.description: notaio's signed bundles, one ConfigMap per policy in each namespace listed in policy.namespaces. State notaio owns and the broker only reads: the broker's RBAC there is a Role granting get, list and watch on ConfigMaps and nothing else. A bundle is used only once it verifies against the configured keys at the current time and passes notaio's floor rule; one that fails is logged with its reason and changes nothing, an expired one leaves the cache. Under policy.egress: shadow (the default) a bundle is compared with the broker's configuration and reported, never enforced (ADR-0026, roadmap 09, done); under policy.egress: enforce its servable direct egress is served at the gateway (ADR-0030), and a gateway-placed audience must be one the claim's policy admits (ADR-0040). Which namespaces' bundles a sandbox may name is the broker's configuration, policy.sources (ADR-0054), never cluster state: a namespace's own bundles by default, an explicit list otherwise; being read (policy.namespaces) does not make a bundle nameable.

nodes.name: SandboxAudience bundles (ConfigMaps)
nodes.description: notaio's signed audience bundles (notaio ADR-0020, mediatore ADR-0055): one <audience>-audience ConfigMap per SandboxAudience, the envelope under audience.dsse.json, in the platform audience namespace (platform audiences, visible from every namespace) or a sandbox namespace (team audiences, usable only from that namespace). The kind is the namespace's, never a field of the bundle. Read with the same Role and keys as the policy bundles; verified under the audience payload type, so a policy bundle never verifies as one nor the reverse; a version floor per audience in the store beside the policy floors. Checked again on admission (a team audience's backend is secret or none and never OpenBao, no reserved header, exact DNS endpoints), and a name or endpoint two audiences share is refused for both from every namespace that sees both. Under policy.audience_definitions.mode: shadow they are compared with audiences[] and logged; the file still serves. The credentials they name are read under shadow too (rel-mediatore-audience-secrets, rel-mediatore-openbao-audience-kv) and only the outcome logged; the bundles mode and the API's use of the catalog are decided (ADR-0055) and not built.

nodes.name: Policy trust anchor (configured keys)
nodes.description: policy.trusted_keys in the broker's configuration: the Ed25519 public keys, by notaio's key id, that a bundle must be signed with. Configuration, never cluster state, so whoever can write objects in the cluster cannot choose the policy; two versions listed cover a rotation. A key that does not decode to 32 bytes or a duplicate id refuses the start; a missing policy section turns the whole of ADR-0026 off (built: crates/mediatore/src/config.rs).

nodes.name: SPIRE Server (downstream)
nodes.description: The environment-scoped SPIRE server: holds the TPM attestor, the EK trust bundle and the k8s_psat config for this cluster, and issues node identities and workload SVIDs. Its registration entries are rendered by the SPIRE Controller Manager in the same pod over a private Unix socket; no admin API is reachable over the network. mediatore's two entry kinds (/banlieue/node/<ek-hash>, /banlieue/claim/<uid>, ADR-0004) arrive as ClusterStaticEntry resources (ADR-0006). In the enterprise topology it chains to the root via an intermediate CA; in the homelab it is the whole tree (ADR-0005), its CA since ADR-0031 an intermediate signed by OpenBao's PKI engine (deploy/spire-upstream: the vault UpstreamAuthority with a projected ServiceAccount token, audience openbao), so agents anchor on a root that outlives it. The TPM node attestor is spiffe/spire-tpm-plugin as a kustomize component (deploy/spire-tpm: an init container from the digest-pinned image, the checksum in server.conf) and its EK trust bundle is one swtpm local CA issuing certificate per hypervisor host, copied beside the plugin by the init container (ADR-0018).

nodes.name: SPIRE Controller Manager
nodes.description: Runs beside the SPIRE server in the same pod (leader-elected across replicas). Watches ClusterSPIFFEID and ClusterStaticEntry resources and renders them into server registration entries over a private Unix socket. The only writer of entries in the cluster; reports status.rendered / masked / set on each resource (ADR-0006).

nodes.name: ClusterStaticEntry resources
nodes.description: Cluster-scoped declarations of mediatore's registration entries: mediatore-node-<ek-hash> and mediatore-claim-<uid>, labelled app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=mediatore. Shape enforced at admission by CEL policy: spiffeID under /banlieue/, parentID a tpm agent with the same EK hash, unix selectors only, no admin/downstream/storeSVID. Auditable through the API server audit log and restorable from a cluster backup (ADR-0006).

nodes.name: SPIRE Agent + SPIFFE CSI driver (k8s node)
nodes.description: Per-node DaemonSets from the hardened chart. The agent attests the node with k8s_psat, attests pods through a kubelet whose serving certificate it verifies, and serves the Workload API on a hostPath socket directory. The CSI driver bind-mounts that directory read-only into pods that declare a csi.spiffe.io inline volume, so no workload needs a hostPath. Both are node-level TCB, the same tier as the kubelet (ADR-0007).

nodes.name: SPIRE Root Server (desired state)
nodes.description: Root of the trust domain on the dedicated identity cluster: HA, PostgreSQL-backed, CA keyed through an UpstreamAuthority plugin against an HSM / KMS / corporate PKI. Issues intermediate CAs to downstream servers only; no agent or workload talks to it directly. Elided in the homelab collapse (ADR-0005).

nodes.name: Identity Cluster (desired state)
nodes.description: Dedicated cluster (auth.example.com style) owned by the identity/security team, with its own change control. Hosts only the SPIRE root and its datastore; sandbox-cluster administrators have no access here (ADR-0005).

nodes.name: Management Cluster
nodes.description: The banlieue management cluster: runs mediatore, the downstream SPIRE server with its controller manager, the SPIRE agent and SPIFFE CSI driver DaemonSets, the Kubernetes API and the banlieue controllers. In the homelab this is the single banlieue cluster and the downstream server is the only SPIRE server.

nodes.name: Sandbox VM (pool member)
nodes.description: A banlieue pool member with a fresh vTPM, attested at boot before any claim exists. Boots the sandbox VM image, a Kairos Debian derivative built from this repository (image/Dockerfile, published as ghcr.io/firestoned/mediatore-guest, signed and attested; ADR-0023): the one mediatore binary at /usr/bin/mediatore, the SPIRE agent and its TPM attestor plugin in the immutable rootfs, nftables, tpm2-tools, qemu-guest-agent, no sshd or other listener; the agent's configuration and the trust bundle from the deployment's cloud-config layer at every boot, the agent's key on the sealed persistent partition, never in the image. Carries the in-guest agent and, once bound, the jailed workload. Its units start only on the installed disk, and its GuestReady is announced by the in-guest agent after registration (ADR-0019), not by a boot stage. With egress gateways, the pool's cloud-config layer points the agent's server_address and MEDIATORE_URL at a gateway's sandbox address and the control relay's ports, by address, and writes the bootstrap list /etc/mediatore/gateways the guest uses until the broker's gateways arrive (ADR-0027 decisions 3 and 4). With gateways the image also loads inet mediatore_host from the pool's own files (which, for a pool with a gateway-placed audience, include MEDIATORE_INJECT_PORT: each gateway admitted at it for every uid, ADR-0040 decision 13) before the agent and the guest (image/host-table, mediatore-host-nft.service, ADR-0029): the bound on root and every uid, names refused; /etc/mediatore/registries names the mirror and MEDIATORE_REGISTRY_CA its CA.

nodes.name: SPIRE Agent (in guest)
nodes.description: Attests the node with the vTPM EK certificate and serves the Workload API socket to the guest and to the egress proxy outside the jail; since ADR-0025 the jail has no socket and reaches the proxy alone.

nodes.name: mediatore guest
nodes.description: Root daemon, the guest role of the one mediatore binary (ADR-0014): registers the node (EK hash + DMI UUID), then announces GuestReady to the hypervisor over the channel banlieue reads (the /run marker, guestinfo or vsock; ADR-0019), so the pool counts the member only once it is attested and registered; polls GET /v1/me for a bound claim, creates the per-subject user (sb- + 12 hex, ADR-0004), mounts a size-bounded tmpfs at /mnt/sandbox (nosuid, nodev, mode 0711 so the egress proxy reaches its files; ADR-0021 amended) and pulls the claim's workload image from its registry into it as the rootfs (with the operator's credential for that registry when the broker handed one over, used for the pull and kept nowhere; ADR-0022), manifest and layers verified against their digests, the manifest digest logged (ADR-0021), loads the per-claim nftables ruleset keyed by that uid (the broker, the audiences' egress endpoints, DNS; no ruleset, no jail; ADR-0020), bind-mounts the binary at the pinned path read-only into the jail and supervises the nsjail until the deadline, restarting the workload as its restart policy says (ADR-0033: always, on-failure, never) and, when the policy ends the claim, telling the broker how the workload exited (POST /v1/me/exit) so the claim is released, then tears down; what nsjail execs is the binary's jail-exec role, which applies Landlock to itself (the rootfs readable, /work, /tmp and the home writable, TCP connect to the egress proxy's port only, no bind) before the workload's argv runs, and a refusal (exit 125) ends the claim instead of restarting (ADR-0024). Since ADR-0025 it also generates the claim's phantom token, writes the routes GET /v1/me returned to a file of the sandbox user's, starts mediatore egress-proxy as that user outside the jail before the jail, and ends the claim if the proxy exits. crates/mediatore-guest. The ruleset has two shapes since ADR-0028 decision 6 (net::Shape): with gateways, from GET /v1/me or the pool's /etc/mediatore/gateways, the relay, the gateways and the proxy by address and no DNS rule at all, a broker or gateway given by name refusing the claim; without, ADR-0020's list, the broker, the audiences' endpoints resolved at load, the proxy and DNS. The pull trusts the mirror's CA beside the Mozilla roots when told (MEDIATORE_REGISTRY_CA, ADR-0029). Since ADR-0045, for a claim whose requester opted in (workload.logs), it spawns the jail with piped stdout and stderr, redacts every line before it leaves the VM (crates/mediatore-guest/src/redact.rs, logs.rs: the phantom and every secret-bearing environment value, and JWTs, Authorization values and private keys by shape; best effort, not a guarantee), writes the redacted copy to the console, and ships batches to the broker over the node SVID without ever blocking the workload; the last batch is flushed before the exit is reported.

nodes.name: Jailed Workload
nodes.description: Runs under nsjail as the per-subject user in a read-only rootfs unpacked from the claim's image onto a per-claim tmpfs (ADR-0021), with only the binary mounted in and /work writable, in the VM's network namespace behind an nftables chain keyed by its uid (ADR-0020); and under Landlock, applied by its own process before the first instruction of the workload (mediatore jail-exec, ADR-0024): writes only to /work, /tmp and the home whatever the image's file modes say, TCP connect to the egress proxy's loopback port and no other, no TCP bind, signals and abstract sockets scoped to the jail, inherited by every child. And a third layer in the same process (ADR-0051, crates/mediatore-guest/src/seccomp.rs): a seccomp filter applied after Landlock that refuses every socket family but AF_UNIX, AF_INET and AF_INET6, any inet socket that is not a stream, and io_uring, so a vsock, a UDP socket or an io_uring socket operation no longer depends on the nftables chain or on a dropped capability. Holds no credential: since ADR-0025 the Workload API socket is not mounted, the broker is unreachable, and the jail's environment carries MEDIATORE_EGRESS_PROXY (http://127.0.0.1:3128) and MEDIATORE_TOKEN, a phantom the proxy swaps for the real token on the way out. The binary stays mounted read-only for jail-exec (ADR-0014, ADR-0024).

nodes.name: mediatore egress-proxy
nodes.description: The egress-proxy role of the one binary (ADR-0025), one process per claim started by the guest as the sandbox user outside the jail, in the VM's namespace and filesystem. A reverse proxy on 127.0.0.1:3128: the workload calls /<host>[:<port>]/<path> with the phantom token, the proxy checks the host against the claim's routes (one per audience and egress endpoint, and under policy.egress enforce one per direct egress entry of the claim's bundle the gateway serves, from GET /v1/me) and the method and path against the route's rules (nono's endpoint_rules shape: method or *, a path glob with * one segment and ** any), swaps the phantom for a token for the route's audience fetched over the claim SVID at POST /v1/token and cached until shortly before its expiry, or on a route with credential none (a bundle's direct entry, an audience via: none; ADR-0025 decision 8) drops the phantom and forwards bare; for an audience via: secret (ADR-0032) the credential is the operator's, placed in the header the broker named (Authorization as a bearer, or x-api-key and the like) with the extra headers beside it, the phantom recognised in that header too and every owned header stripped on every route; and forwards over TLS 1.3 to the Mozilla roots, or to the CA the route carries for an audience on a private PKI (audiences[].ca_file, ADR-0025 decision 7). No TLS interception. A request with no Authorization header is forwarded bare, one with a foreign bearer is 401 on every route, one outside the rules 403, one to a host not in the routes 404. In an environment with egress gateways (the gateways list on GET /v1/me, ADR-0028 decision 6) the upstream is not dialled directly: the proxy's dialer is the forwarder of ADR-0028 decision 3, placed in this process by ADR-0027 decision 8 (crates/mediatore-guest/src/forward.rs): TLS 1.3 to a gateway on the sandbox leg's configuration presenting the claim SVID and verifying spiffe://<td>/gateway, CONNECT host:port, the upstream's TLS inside the tunnel; the list walked from a random start per connection, a connect or handshake failure moving to the next (decision 7), a gateway's refusal final (502 gateway_refused at the workload, the authorizer's code in the log; 502 gateway_unreachable when none carried it). The only process that ever holds a downstream token or the claim SVID; the uid-keyed table drops packets to its port from any other uid, and a proxy that exits ends the claim. crates/mediatore-guest/src/egress.rs. ADR-0040: on a route with credential: gateway the proxy never fetches a token; it sends the request in origin form to the gateway's inject port over the claim-SVID mutual TLS and the gateway places the credential.

nodes.name: Egress gateway (Envoy + mediatore gateway, with the control relay beside them)
nodes.description: The egress gateway of ADR-0028 on each of banlieue's three proxy VMs per environment (banlieue ADR-0109), built as image content (image/gateway/, published as ghcr.io/firestoned/mediatore-gateway, signed and attested; the VMs, the two-interface class and the entries in deploy/gateway/). The data plane: Envoy on the sandbox address, mutual TLS 1.3 with X25519MLKEM768 offered first, its own identity spiffe://<td>/gateway over SDS from the local SPIRE agent (the VM attests with its vTPM like a pool member; ClusterStaticEntry objects per VM applied by the platform team, one per user: unix:user:envoy and, with inject, unix:user:envoy-inject for spiffe://<td>/gateway, and unix:user:mediatore-gateway for the authorizer's own identity spiffe://<td>/gateway/authorizer, ADR-0053, its client identity to the broker, selected by path and required at start; an admission policy pins the two shapes, deploy/base/admission/clusterstaticentry-gateway.yaml; the host table's output chain, keyed on the socket's owner, admits the broker's address to the authorizer's and the relay's users alone and refuses both Envoys loopback, link-local, the control-plane addresses and IPv6, image/gateway/nftables.conf.in), every peer required to be a claim of the trust domain before any filter runs, CONNECT the only route, each tunnel checked with the authorizer beside it, mediatore gateway (crates/mediatore-gateway: Envoy's own Check call over gRPC on loopback; the peer from the verified certificate, the method and the authority; OK or PERMISSION_DENIED with a stable code from a bounded cache of one allowlist per claim, fresh 30 s, stale for 300 s more while the broker is unreachable, never past the claim's deadline, dropped on the broker's 404, least recently used evicted past 4096 claims, one ask per claim at a time, deny on no answer), the authority resolved and dialled by Envoy from the egress address, one access-log line per tunnel keyed by the peer's SPIFFE ID, no admin interface, no interception. The host: forwarding off, an nftables table with default-drop input admitting the data port and the relay ports on the sandbox interface only, nothing new on egress, both Envoys as their own users with no capability and a read-only root (ADR-0028 decision 8, ADR-0027 decision 5). The bootstrap the kind tier proves is the image's template rendered with the tier's values (make kind-e2e-gateway, make gateway-render-check). The image is built and checked (image/gateway/check.sh) and runs live on the gateway VMs since 2026-11-05 (roadmap 10). ADR-0040 (implemented): where an audience is declared inject: gateway the authorizer also answers a second question on a second unix socket, for envoy-inject (a third Envoy process beside the data plane and the relay), obtains the credential from the broker (POST /v1/gateway/claims/{uid}/credential) and returns it only to that Envoy in the check response; the data-plane socket never returns one.

nodes.name: Control relay (Envoy, no identity)
nodes.description: ADR-0027's control plane on each gateway VM: a second Envoy, its own systemd unit and user (envoy-relay, image/gateway/systemd/envoy-relay.service), with no SPIRE socket (InaccessiblePaths=/run/spire), no SVID and no credential of any kind. Four tcp_proxy listeners on the sandbox address, 3129 to the SPIRE server's attestation port, 3130 to the broker's sandbox listener, 3131 (ADR-0037) to the SPIRE servers' bundle endpoint and 3132 (ADR-0038) to the operator's registry, each a fixed upstream by address from the deployment's env file (image/gateway/envoy/relay.yaml.in): no CONNECT, no authority from the client, no name resolution for the sandbox. It carries the pool VM's bootstrap connections as ciphertext, the TLS end to end between the agent and the server, between the node or the claim and the broker, between the boot-time bundle fetch and the bundle endpoint (its web PKI certificate, checked by the member against the endpoint's hostname), and between the guest's image pull and the registry (the registry's own certificate, checked against its own name; admitted by the host table to uid 0 alone, never in the jail's table), and sees only metadata, which it logs one line per connection (source, upstream, bytes each way, duration). The host table bounds each sandbox source's new relay connections (ct count over RELAY_CAP in a dynamic set, ADR-0027 decision 5), since the relay has no identity to rate-limit by. It is the only way a pool VM reaches the identity plane: the segment has no route and no resolver.

nodes.name: Downstream APIs
nodes.description: Services the sandbox may call on the user's behalf: Entra-protected APIs (OBO tokens) or JWKS-validating services (STS tokens with the act claim). Each validates audience and can audit 'broker on behalf of user'.

nodes.name: Workload Image Registry
nodes.description: The OCI registry the claim's workload.image names (ghcr.io, Docker Hub, a registry on the segment). The guest pulls from it over HTTPS, anonymously or with the operator's credential from the broker's config (ADR-0022), with the distribution API, follows one bearer challenge, verifies every blob against its digest and logs the manifest digest that ran; a tag is the registry's word, a digest pin is the requester's (ADR-0021). Trusted for availability, not for content. In an environment with egress gateways it is the operator's registry or pull-through mirror with an address on the sandbox segment (ADR-0029 decision 1), declared on the broker with registries[].reach: segment (a credential optional) and on the pool in /etc/mediatore/registries; a claim naming any other registry is refused before it exists, and the images a pool runs are the ones the operator mirrored.

nodes.name: Sandbox Network Segment
nodes.description: Pool members' network, layer 2 only (banlieue ADR-0109): no route anywhere and no resolver. A member reaches exactly the three gateways' sandbox addresses: the data plane (TCP 8443, mutual TLS with the claim SVID, CONNECT to the claim's allowlist) and the control relay (TCP 3129 to the SPIRE server, 3130 to the broker, 3131 to the bundle endpoint, ADR-0037, and 3132 to the operator's registry for root's pull alone, ADR-0038; the TLS inside end to end). The SPIRE server, the broker's sandbox listener, the workload image registry and the downstream APIs are reached through the gateways and never directly; from inside the jail the sandbox uid reaches the egress proxy on loopback alone, and the proxy's own sockets the relay and the gateways by address (ADR-0020 as amended by ADR-0028 decision 6 and ADR-0027 decision 6). Nothing inbound to a VM. In an environment without gateways yet, the older shape: the broker, the audiences' egress endpoints and the resolvers. The workload image registry a gateway-era pool pulls from is on this segment too, a registry or pull-through mirror at layer 2 (ADR-0029 decision 1): a public registry is unreachable by construction. Every uid on a member is bounded by the image's host table, input and forward dropped, output to the gateways' two planes and the segment's registries alone (ADR-0029 decision 3).

nodes.name: envoy-inject (credential placement Envoy, ADR-0040)
nodes.description: ADR-0040's third Envoy on each gateway VM, only where an audience is declared inject: gateway: its own systemd unit and static user (envoy-inject), no admin interface, its own SPIRE entry for the gateway SPIFFE ID (unix:user:envoy-inject, one entry per user). One listener on the sandbox address and its own port (INJECT_PORT, admitted by the gateway's nftables table to the sandbox range under the per-source cap): mutual TLS 1.3 with the claim SAN prefix required, HTTP/1.1, no CONNECT route, no dynamic forward proxy. A route matches the request's :authority exactly against the one upstream the env file names (INJECT_HOST, INJECT_UPSTREAM_PORT, INJECT_DOMAIN; a second upstream is a second virtual host and cluster in the template, a reviewed change like a relay leg, never a parameter) and goes to a static cluster with TLS origination (SNI the host; system roots, or a PEM for a private PKI); a host not in the list has no route (404). ext_authz on the listener asks the authorizer on inject/inject.sock (group envoy-inject) with context_extensions mode inject; the authorizer alone writes the credential header (OVERWRITE_IF_EXISTS_OR_ADD) and removes any a client sent, so no route, virtual-host or listener-level header rule may name the credential header (Envoy applies those after ext_authz; shown on 1.40.2, TESTING.md T-61). Paths are normalised before the authorizer's rules see them (normalize_path, merge_slashes, an escaped slash rejected). The per-claim limit of ADR-0040 decision 5 is not built (a marked placeholder in the template): until it is, the host table's per-source connection cap bounds a sandbox's connections to the port. The credential is in a request's headers for at most the 300 second cap and is never logged (access log without headers, info level, suppress_envoy_headers). The data-plane Envoy and the relay never hold a credential: this is the only Envoy that does. Without a gateway-placed audience it is not started.

nodes.name: The requester's saved credential (OS credential store)
nodes.description: ADR-0041 decision 5, amended by ADR-0043 decision 5: one item per audience in the requester's own OS credential store (the macOS Keychain; service mediatore, account the audience), holding the user name and secret and the time they were saved, created only on an explicit yes (the default is no). Its age limit is the least of six hours and the claim's TTL: an item older than that is deleted and refused, and mediatore logout --audience deletes it. Read and written by the CLI on the requester's machine; never sent anywhere but in the claim body (ADR-0041 decision 3), and the requester's OS decides which other programs may read it. Other platforms have no store source. Status: the six-hour bound is live; the claim-TTL bound (ADR-0043 decision 5) is built and unit-tested, not yet run live.

nodes.name: Workload output (the Secret ring)
nodes.description: ADR-0045: the redacted stdout and stderr of a sandbox whose requester opted in (workload.logs: true), as the broker keeps it: a ring of Secrets in the broker's own namespace, mediatore-logs-<claim uid>-<segment>, 64 KiB of record text per segment, labelled mediatore.io/logs=segment with the claim and sandbox UIDs, owned by the AgentSandbox when it shares the namespace, capped at logs.max_bytes per claim (default 1 MiB, ceiling 4 MiB; the oldest segment dropped and the dropped bytes counted), swept by the leader's resync logs.retention_secs after the claim ended (default: store.retention_secs). Since ADR-0052 each segment's entries are sealed per ingested batch with the broker's OpenBao transit key (the same mount, key and role as the sessions, a separate derivation context bound to the claim UID and the output's purpose): one blob per line, with only the sequence range, the record text byte count and the key id in clear, the segment marked mediatore.io/seal=v1; at most 64 KiB of record text per blob, so a maximum batch is at most 5 transit calls. Each stored unit, once opened, is a LogRecord {seq, stream, ts, text} or a LogGap {lost_stdout, lost_stderr, unreadable}. Readable through the broker by the claim's owner alone (the same subject check as GET /v1/claims/{name}); an unreachable sealer is a 503 on ingest and on read and never a plaintext fallback, a blob that does not open for the claim or a segment without the seal marker is served as an unreadable gap and never as output, and logs.enabled without store.sealing refuses to start. A cluster administrator reading the Secrets directly sees ciphertext; acting as the broker at OpenBao is what decrypts (threat model R-39, narrowed). Redaction happened in the VM and is best effort (R-38): the ring is a Secret, not a ConfigMap, because it may hold what redaction missed. In memory under dev_mode with the same cap, cursor and sweep rules (LogRing, crates/mediatore-store). Nothing is stored for a sandbox that did not opt in or on a broker with logs.enabled false.

nodes.name: Per-host signing CA bundle (x509pop trust anchors, ADR-0049)
nodes.description: Decided, not built (ADR-0049, Proposed). The x509pop NodeAttestor's ca_bundle_path on the SPIRE server: one CA certificate per host whose guests have no vTPM, each created at the host's install and held (key included) only by that host's provider; the certificate is public and an operator adds it to the bundle when onboarding the host, never discovered from the host. Controls: (1) every CA in the bundle has a UNIQUE, operator-chosen common name and the bundle's rendering refuses a duplicate (mediatore-spire refuse_duplicate_common_names), because the agent ID is issuer-qualified and a duplicate removes the confinement; (2) the server's agent_path_template is /x509pop/{{ .Issuer.CommonName }}/{{ .Subject.CommonName }}, giving the agent ID spiffe://<td>/spire/agent/x509pop/<issuer CN>/<subject CN>, stable across certificate renewal and declarable before the guest boots, with both common names restricted to the path-segment alphabet (mediatore-spire x509pop_agent_id); (3) the host's signer ignores the CSR subject and sets the subject CN to the VM's UID, basicConstraints CA:FALSE (the server does not enforce it) and keyUsage digitalSignature (the server requires it), with a bounded validity; (4) a compromised host can speak only for its own guests, under its own CA's name; (5) retiring a CA revokes every identity it signed at the agents' next re-attestation. No SPIRE admin identity and no join token: mediatore still only declares ClusterStaticEntry (ADR-0006). The TPM attestor and its EK CA bundle (ADR-0018) are unchanged and stay the attestor of every guest with a vTPM.

relationships.description: The mediatore system is one binary composed of the two API surfaces, the claim watcher and the STS; the claim store and the STS signing key are the state it guards, with the configured policy keys the trust anchor for notaio's bundles (ADR-0026).

Everything identity-bearing on a pool member: the SPIRE agent (node identity), the in-guest agent (subject plumbing), the egress proxy (claim identity, the tokens) and the jailed workload (a phantom token and one loopback route).

Pool members live on the layer 2 sandbox segment; the gateways and their control relay have their sandbox interface on it and their egress interface on a routable network (banlieue ADR-0109 decision 4).

Everything control-plane-side shares the management cluster; the SPIRE downstream server, its controller manager and the per-node agent and CSI driver are scoped to it so entry rendering, k8s_psat validation and pod attestation stay per-environment.
The root SPIRE server lives alone on the identity cluster; the root signing key never resides where sandboxes are administered.

Nested SPIRE: the downstream server obtains its intermediate CA from the root and chains every SVID it issues to the one trust domain. Revoking the intermediate cuts an entire environment off from above. Absent in the homelab collapse (ADR-0005).
The user logs in at the IdP (PKCE via mediatore login or az login) and receives a token whose audience is mediatore. The user's token is only ever presented to mediatore, never to the VM.

POST /v1/claims with the IdP bearer token creates an AgentSandbox with the token's subject (ADR-0008); GET answers from its status, DELETE deletes it. Subject equality is enforced on read and delete, and the caller must be in the claim's namespace's groups for create, read and delete alike (ADR-0046): a person who left the group can no longer read or delete through the broker, and a cluster administrator's kubectl delete is the break-glass path. The request may name a namespace (ClaimRequest.namespace, ClaimResponse.namespace). For a via: delegated audience (ADR-0035) the request carries the caller's own credential for it (the CLI reads Claude Code's session, a variable or a file), sealed with the AgentSandbox UID into a Secret of its own beside the session's and opened only at POST /v1/token for the proxy; a claim naming such an audience without it is refused. For a session issuer the request also carries the caller's refresh token (mediatore login, PKCE as client mediatore; ADR-0013), which is sealed with the AgentSandbox UID into a sessions row before the response and follows the claim into its record; it never touches the resource. Since ADR-0045, GET /v1/claims/{name}/logs?follow=&since=&tail= streams the stored output of a claim created with workload.logs: true as NDJSON (a header with the dropped byte count and the phase, the records and gaps in sequence, an end line) to the claim's owner under the same subject and namespace checks, 501 when the broker's logs section is off, 503 when the store cannot be read; a follower is re-read when a batch for its claim is stored through this replica and at least every two seconds, with an empty keepalive line every fifteen; every read is one audit line with the claim UID and subject and never the content. A POST /v1/claims with workload.logs: true on a broker with logs.enabled false is refused 501 before anything is created.

JWKS discovery and signature validation for incoming tokens; for a session issuer (ADR-0013, built), a refresh_token grant before every token issue, as mediatore's own public client: the fresh ID token is validated like a login (group gate included), the rotated refresh token re-sealed into the record, and invalid_grant releases the claim at once. For an Entra issuer (ADR-0016, built): the On-Behalf-Of exchange of the caller's access token at claim creation (offline_access, the first entra-obo audience or mediatore's own resource), mediatore authenticating with a PS256 client assertion signed by a key file, by OpenBao transit, or presented as a projected ServiceAccount token under workload identity federation; before every issue a refresh_token grant naming the audience's resource, a token for mediatore itself validated like a login for an sts audience, Entra's token handed to the workload as is for an entra-obo audience. The user's original token is discarded after validation.

Creates the AgentSandbox, in the namespace the broker resolved from the token's groups and its namespace map (ADR-0046; the ServiceAccount can create in all of them, so the map is the control on the broker's front door and does not govern the declarative path), with spec.subject from the validated token (ADR-0008); the reconciler, not the user API, creates the VirtualMachineClaim. The mediatore ServiceAccount is exempt from the caller-equals-subject check of the agentsandbox-subject policy because it acts for subjects it has validated tokens for, and is listed as a broker in banlieue's claim-subject policy.

Watches VirtualMachineClaim (label app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=mediatore) for Bound / Releasing / Failed / deletion and VirtualMachine (banlieue.io/pool) for a published vTPM endorsement certificate; binds by the EK hash the claim mirrors, fails an unresolved bind after 60 s by deleting the claim, declares node entries from members (ADR-0011). Runs on the replica holding the coordination.k8s.io Lease mediatore-watcher.

Watches AgentSandbox and creates, owns and deletes its one VirtualMachineClaim through the Kubernetes API with the broker ServiceAccount (ADR-0008, built). RBAC: get/list/watch/patch/create/delete on agentsandboxes, patch on agentsandboxes/status and update on agentsandboxes/finalizers; create/delete/get/list/watch on virtualmachineclaims. Never patches a pool member: binding stays in banlieue's claim controller.

Collects the SandboxNode of a VM that no longer exists (ADR-0039, built): once per resync, on the replica holding the Lease, lists the pool member VirtualMachines (get/list/watch on virtualmachines, already granted) and deletes a SandboxNode whose EK hash no VM publishes (delete on sandboxnodes, already granted). Never a banned node, a node younger than store.node_grace_secs (600 s by default), a node an unended claim is bound to, or more than 20 per pass; an empty VM list is not believed while a node is young or a claim is active; a failed listing removes nothing.
An AgentSandbox is the sandbox user's request, attributed to them by admission; the claim, entry and tokens all derive from it.
banlieue's claim controller binds Ready pool members to claims and destroys members on release; mediatore only observes the results. CRDs are the entire interface.

Declares the claim entry (parent = the bound VM's tpm agent ID, selector unix:user:sb-<hash>) as a ClusterStaticEntry on Bound and deletes it on release, through the Kubernetes API with the broker ServiceAccount. RBAC: create/delete/get/list/watch on clusterstaticentries only; the mediatore-clusterstaticentry admission policy rejects any other shape. Waits for status.set. No gRPC, no admin SVID (ADR-0006).

notaio writes each policy's bundle ConfigMap in the policy's namespace and keeps it current: a new version on every change, re-signed on a key rotation (ADR-0026); and each SandboxAudience's bundle ConfigMap in the audience's namespace, once its platform audience namespace is set (notaio ADR-0020, mediatore ADR-0055). mediatore never calls notaio; the ConfigMap is the whole interface.

The bundle reflector (ADR-0026 decision 3, implemented): a watch on ConfigMaps labelled app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=notaio in each namespace of policy.namespaces, with a Role per namespace granting get, list and watch on ConfigMaps and nothing else. A ConfigMap without bundle.dsse.json, or whose envelope does not parse, is logged and ignored. The condition the comparison writes goes through rel-watcher-agentsandboxes, on agentsandboxes/status.

The audience reflector (ADR-0055 decision 1, built for shadow): a watch on ConfigMaps labelled app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=notaio in the platform audience namespace and every sandbox namespace, under the policy bundles' Role (get, list and watch on ConfigMaps only). A ConfigMap without audience.dsse.json is a policy bundle or not notaio's and is skipped. Every replica runs it, outside the Lease; the SandboxAudience CRD is never read.

A team audience's credential, or a platform audience's secretRef (ADR-0055 decision 5, built; read under shadow and logged, served once bundles is built): get on one named Secret in the audience's own namespace, polled every credential_refresh_secs, through a Role with resourceNames per namespace (deploy/audience-credentials), created at onboarding and never by the broker. No list, no watch, no write.
The policy and audience bundles are notaio's state; mediatore holds a verified copy in memory and the floors in its store.
Watches ClusterSPIFFEID and ClusterStaticEntry resources and reports rendering status on them.

Unix domain socket, not a network protocol (CALM's protocol enum has no value for it). Renders declared resources into registration entries over the server's private Unix socket inside the pod. The admin API is never exposed on the network.

Unix domain socket, not a network protocol (CALM's protocol enum has no value for it). The broker pod fetches spiffe://<td>/mediatore and the trust-domain bundle from the node's SPIRE agent over the Workload API socket, mounted read-only by the SPIFFE CSI driver (no hostPath). SVID and key stay in process memory and rotate on the stream (ADR-0007).
k8s_psat node attestation with a projected, audience-bound ServiceAccount token, then SVID fetching for attested pods.

TPM node attestation at boot (EK certificate + credential activation), then SVID rotation. Claim-independent: a warm member is attested before any claim exists. With egress gateways the agent's server_address is a gateway's sandbox address and the relay's SPIRE port (ADR-0027 decision 3): the attestation's TLS is end to end, the relay sees ciphertext. One address, so the agent fails over between gateways only when it restarts (ADR-0027's open item).

POST /v1/nodes (EK hash + DMI UUID + hostname) over the node SVID at boot; then polls GET /v1/me until a claim is bound and the subject comes back. Since ADR-0022 the answer to GET /v1/me includes the pull credential for the claim's image registry when the operator configured one. Since ADR-0025 it carries the proxy's routes, and since ADR-0025 decision 8 (2026-11-08) a route may carry credential none: one per served direct egress entry of the claim's bundle under policy.egress enforce, with no audience, and the routes of an audience via: none. Since ADR-0028 decision 6 the answer also carries gateways, the environment's egress gateways in the broker's order, for the forwarder and the ruleset; empty until the gateways exist. With egress gateways the connection itself runs through a gateway's control relay (ADR-0027 decision 3), the node SVID's mutual TLS end to end inside it, and the guest falls back to the pool's bootstrap list /etc/mediatore/gateways when the answer lists none (decision 4). Once the image is pulled and the tables are loaded, before the jail, the guest POSTs /v1/me/report over the same identity: the manifest digest, the sandbox ruleset's hash and the host table as nft lists it, hashed, or its absence (ADR-0029 decision 5); the broker keeps it on the claim's record (logged when the claim is swept), and GET /v1/claims/{name} shows it. Since ADR-0045, when GET /v1/me says workload.logs the guest also POSTs /v1/me/logs over the node SVID: batches of the jailed workload's stdout and stderr lines, redacted in the VM (the phantom and every secret-bearing environment value literally and in their base64 and percent-encoded forms; JWTs, Authorization values and private-key PEM blocks by shape), on the leading edge (at once after a quiet half second, otherwise every half second, or at 32 KiB; a line that has not ended after 150 ms of silence as a partial record, less the end the redactor holds back), with a per-claim sequence number the broker uses to accept a retried batch idempotently and per-stream dropped byte counts when the guest's 1 MiB queue overflowed; the workload never waits for the broker, a 429 is honoured, a 501 or 404 stops shipping for the claim and keeps the console copy, and the last batch is flushed, bounded to five seconds, before POST /v1/me/exit. The broker accepts a batch from the claim's node alone, re-validates its shape and size (400, 413), rate-limits it to two per second (429), refuses one for a claim that did not opt in (400 logs_not_requested), and answers 501 with logs.enabled off.

After POST /v1/nodes is accepted, the installed-guest announcement banlieue ADR-0043 defines, on the channel its provider reads: /run/banlieue/phase (libvirt, through qemu-guest-agent), guestinfo.banlieue.phase (vSphere), phase=installed over vsock (Cloud Hypervisor). Liveness only; mediatore reads it nowhere (ADR-0019).

The in-guest agent, as root and before the ruleset is loaded, pulls the claim's workload image: the manifest (an index resolved to linux/<arch>) and the layers, each verified against its digest, applied in order with whiteouts into the rootfs on the per-claim tmpfs; nothing escapes the rootfs, setuid bits are dropped, device nodes skipped (ADR-0021). HTTPS with WebPKI roots; plain HTTP only for a registry named on the command line, and never with a credential. The credential, when GET /v1/me carried one, goes to the registry's token endpoint as HTTP Basic, or on the content when the registry challenges with Basic (ADR-0022). In a gateway-era environment the registry is the mirror on the segment, reached at layer 2 through the host table's allowance (ADR-0029); the broker refused any other registry at the claim. For a registry that is a placed audience (ADR-0043) the guest does not hold or present a credential at all: the pull goes through the claim's egress proxy and the gateway places it (rel-guest-pull-egress-proxy, rel-envoy-inject-registry); the operator-held credential of ADR-0022 stays for a deployment that accepts it and is not used in a deployment that stores no credential in a Kubernetes Secret.

Plain HTTP on loopback, the jail's only route out (ADR-0025): GET /<host>[:<port>]/<path> with Authorization: Bearer $MEDIATORE_TOKEN, the phantom; the proxy answers 401 for any other bearer, 403 outside the audience's rules, 404 for a host outside the claim's routes. Landlock admits this port only in the workload's process (ADR-0024) and the uid-keyed table drops packets to it from any other uid (ADR-0020).

POST /v1/token over the claim SVID, by the egress proxy since ADR-0025 (the workload before it): one audience per request, from the claim's allowlist, capped at 15 minutes, never a refresh token; fetched when a request needs it and cached until shortly before its expiry. An audience via: none is refused (403 no_credential, ADR-0025 decision 8): its route carries no credential and the proxy never asks. An audience via: secret (ADR-0032) answers the operator's credential read from a mounted Secret at the broker's start, with the header it goes in and expires_at at now plus max_ttl, so the proxy asks again through the same gate; the value is logged nowhere. Rate-limited per claim (token.rate_per_minute, 429 beyond it) ahead of any upstream call (ADR-0013). With egress gateways this connection too runs through a gateway's control relay, the claim SVID's mutual TLS end to end inside it (ADR-0027 decision 3).

GET /v1/gateway/claims/{uid} over SPIFFE mTLS with the authorizer's SVID, spiffe://<td>/gateway/authorizer (ADR-0028 decision 4 as amended by ADR-0053 decision 3: the sandbox listener admits that identity beside node and claim identities, and no longer the listeners' spiffe://<td>/gateway). The answer is the claim's allowlist, the union of its audiences' egress sorted and deduplicated, exactly what GET /v1/me hands the guest, with the claim's deadline; since ADR-0030, when policy.egress is enforce, the union also holds the direct egress of the claim's verified, unexpired notaio bundle (found by the policy uid on the record, exact host:port entries without rules only, and since ADR-0054 only when the bundle's signed namespace is one of the sources of the record's namespace at the time of the ask; a bundle outside them is treated as missing, audience endpoints only, a placed credential refused), and in shadow, the default, only the log differs; a node, a claim, or anything under the gateway path is refused; a pending, released, expired or unknown claim is 404, which the authorizer takes as deny and drop the cache. Nothing is cached broker-side; the authorizer's bounded per-claim cache is the gateway's (crates/mediatore-gateway), asking over this route with a client built per ask from the current SVID, each ask bounded at five seconds.

The forwarder's tunnel (ADR-0028 decisions 3 and 7, a dialer inside the egress proxy by ADR-0027 decision 8): TCP to a gateway's sandbox address and data port, TLS 1.3 on the sandbox leg's configuration (X25519MLKEM768 only) presenting the claim SVID and verifying the gateway as exactly spiffe://<td>/gateway, CONNECT host:port for the upstream the request names, the upstream's own TLS inside the tunnel end to end. The list from GET /v1/me walked from a random start per connection, a connect or handshake failure or the gateway's own 5xx moving to the next (decision 7 as amended 2026-11-09), a 4xx the verdict and final (502 gateway_refused at the workload, the authorizer's code in the log; gateway_unreachable when none carried it). The lists the forwarder is given leave out the host of a gateway-placed audience (ADR-0040 decision 11): the only path to such a host is the inject listener, where the rules are enforced and the credential placed. Proven against a stand-in gateway in crates/mediatore/tests/e2e_forward.rs and against the real Envoy in kind.

The admitted tunnel: Envoy resolves the CONNECT authority on its own resolver and connects from the egress address to the host:port the authorizer allowed for that claim, relaying the bytes untouched (no interception, ADR-0028 decisions 5 and 9); the TLS inside is the proxy's with the downstream API. One access-log line per tunnel: the peer's SPIFFE ID, the authority, the status, the flags, bytes each way.

A pool VM's bootstrap connections, as ciphertext (ADR-0027 decisions 2 and 3, ADR-0037): the SPIRE agent's attestation and renewals to the relay's 3129, the guest's node session and the egress proxy's claim session to its 3130, and the boot-time fetch of the SPIRE bundle (curl, the endpoint's own hostname as the pin) to its 3131, and the guest's image pull (root's, the registry's own name as the pin) to its 3132 (ADR-0038); each sandbox source bounded by the host table's connection cap (decision 5).

The relay's fixed SPIRE upstream, by address, from the gateway's egress interface: the attestation's TLS passes through unread (ADR-0027 decision 3). The network admits the gateways' egress addresses on this port and nothing from the sandbox range.

The relay's fixed bundle upstream, by address, from the gateway's egress interface: the SPIRE servers' bundle endpoint (https_web profile), whose web PKI certificate the pool VM's fetch verifies itself against the endpoint's hostname, so the relay passes the TLS through unread and could not forge the reply (ADR-0037). The network admits the gateways' egress addresses on this port and nothing from the sandbox range.

The relay's fixed registry upstream, by address, from the gateway's egress interface (ADR-0038): the operator's registry, whose certificate the guest's pull verifies against the registry's own name, end to end; the host table admits the leg to uid 0 alone and the jail's ruleset never lists it. The leg cannot restrict paths, so the registry serves one read-only repository of digest-pinned images.

The relay's fixed broker upstream, by address, from the gateway's egress interface: the node's and the claim's mutual TLS with the sandbox listener pass through unread (ADR-0027 decision 3); the broker verifies the peer's SVID exactly as before and sees the relay's source address.

The proxy forwards the workload's request to the downstream API over TLS 1.3 to the Mozilla roots or to the audience's own CA (audiences[].ca_file, carried on the route), at an endpoint the audience's egress list names (audiences[].egress, returned by GET /v1/me as routes; ADR-0020, ADR-0025), the phantom replaced by the audience-scoped token; the API's audit log records both the user and the broker (azp / act). HTTP/1.1, bodies streamed, one upstream connection per request.

The subject a claim is issued for; the user only ever sees their own claims. An ended claim stays on its AgentSandbox for store.retention_secs, then is swept with the audit line in the log (ADR-0034). Since ADR-0045 the user also reads, through the broker and only for their own claims, the workload output the broker stored (data-asset-workload-output), for the claim's life and its retention window after.

Seal and unseal of refresh material (ADR-0015): encrypt when a session is parked at claim creation, decrypt and encrypt again on every token issue (the refresh of ADR-0013), under a derived transit key with a context that binds the sandbox UID and, since ADR-0057, the slot (the issuer's session, or a delegation with its audience); an envelope sealed before it is bound to the bare UID and still opens. Since ADR-0052 also of a claim's stored workload output: one encrypt per ingested batch (POST /v1/me/logs) and a decrypt for each blob a read of GET /v1/claims/{name}/logs returns (at most four in flight, newest first for a tail, none for blobs behind a cursor), with the context 'mediatore-logs' plus the claim UID so a session ciphertext and an output blob never open as each other; the startup probe covers that context too. The broker logs in with its projected ServiceAccount token (audience openbao) and keeps the OpenBao token in memory until its lease ends. TLS 1.3 verified against store.sealing.transit.ca_file; a probe seal at startup fails the process on a wrong role, policy or key. With issuers[].entra.transit (ADR-0016) the broker also asks transit to sign its client assertion for Entra (PSS, SHA-256) with an RSA key that never leaves OpenBao.

A platform audience's credential (ADR-0055 decision 5, built; read under policy.audience_definitions.mode: shadow and logged, served once bundles is built): a KV v2 read, GET /v1/<mount>/data/<path>, with the same Kubernetes-auth login as transit, configured under policy.audience_definitions.openbao. The mount, path and key come from the signed platform definition; a team audience never names an OpenBao path (notaio L023, refused again by the broker). Read every credential_refresh_secs; a failed read keeps the last good value for two periods, then none. The OpenBao policy grants read on the platform's audience paths and nothing else.
Declared registration entries are state the watcher owns and the controller manager consumes; a sweep deletes any whose claim is gone.

ADR-0031: the server's CA is an intermediate OpenBao's PKI engine signs at root/sign-intermediate every ca_ttl (24h); the server authenticates with a projected ServiceAccount token (Kubernetes auth, audience openbao) to a role whose policy allows that one path, and every signing is in OpenBao's audit log. The trust bundle the server publishes, hence the one a deployment's layer hands every member, is the PKI root: a layer stays good for the root's life, not for one ca_ttl. In the homelab collapse this is the upstream authority ADR-0005 names for the root server.

For a route with credential: gateway (ADR-0040 decision 7) the guest's egress proxy does not tunnel and never calls POST /v1/token: it checks the phantom and the rules as before, strips the phantom, and sends the request in origin form with Host: <audience host> (no port) and no credential, over the claim-SVID mutual TLS 1.3 dialler the forwarder already has, to a gateway's INJECT_PORT (carried on the route by GET /v1/me), streaming the body and returning the response unchanged, failing over to the next gateway on a connection failure only; a response carrying x-mediatore-refusal is the gateway's own refusal and becomes 502 gateway_refused (ADR-0040 decision 12). The workload and the jail are untouched; the sandbox uid's table gains gateway:INJECT_PORT for a claim with such a route and only then, and the pool VM's host table (MEDIATORE_INJECT_PORT in the guest env) admits each gateway at that port for every uid (decision 13). ADR-0043 adds one use: the guest's pull of a private image goes by the same route, as a read-only request to the registry's host (rel-guest-pull-egress-proxy).

The gateway originates TLS to the audience (ADR-0040 decision 3), only for an exact authority in the fixed INJECT_ENDPOINTS list and only after the authorizer's OK: the request leaves with the credential header the authorizer wrote. No certificate authority is minted or trusted for the workload's traffic anywhere: this is origination to a fixed list for an opt-in audience, not interception of a tunnel (ADR-0028 decision 9 stays). The gateway's routable interface must be allowed to reach the host by the datacenter's firewall (an external control).

envoy-inject's ext_authz call (ADR-0040 decisions 4 and 6): gRPC over a unix socket, inject/inject.sock (a directory of its own, setgid 2750 owned by mediatore-gateway and the group envoy-inject so the socket inherits that group, socket 0660; the authorizer's flags are --check-socket, --inject-socket and --socket-dir-mode 2750, and the two sockets never share a directory), the only channel on which the authorizer answers an inject question. The check carries what Envoy fills from the verified connection and the request (source.principal, method, host, path), never read from the client; the answer is OK with the credential header and extra headers, or the same 403 and stable code as for a tunnel, every refusal carrying x-mediatore-refusal: <code> (ADR-0040 decision 12) so the guest can tell the gateway's own refusal from the upstream's 403. The data-plane Envoy's own socket (check/check.sock, group envoy) can only get OK or 403, never a credential, so a compromised tunnel Envoy cannot obtain one even holding the gateway SVID.

POST /v1/gateway/claims/{uid}/credential over SPIFFE mTLS with the authorizer's SVID (ADR-0040 decision 2, ADR-0053 decision 3), body { audience }. Accepted only from spiffe://<td>/gateway/authorizer, runs the checks of POST /v1/token (the claim is live and names the audience, the same per-claim rate limit), requires the audience to be inject: gateway, and adds the policy admission /v1/token does not have (under policy.egress enforce the claim must name a policy whose verified bundle lists the audience, failing closed; shadow logs and allows), and calls the same per-backend code (secret, delegated opened from its sealed envelope, or sts); the answer carries the credential header and value (a Secret, never printed or logged), the non-secret extra headers and an expires_at at most 300 seconds ahead. POST /v1/token for such an audience is 403 placed_at_gateway, so the claim SVID on the pool VM cannot obtain the credential either. One log line per issue: claim UID, audience, subject, backend, expires_at, never the credential. The authorizer holds the answer in memory for at most min(60 s, expires_at minus 30 s).

The CLI reads and writes the saved item (--delegate <audience>=store) and asks for the secret at an echo-off terminal prompt (--delegate <audience>=prompt, terminal only, echo switched off through stty). No flag takes the secret, and no source reads a browser or another application's store (ADR-0041 decisions 4 to 6). TB-18 in the threat model.

ADR-0043 decision 3, for a registry that is a placed audience only: the guest starts the claim's egress proxy (the sandbox user, the claim's SVID) before the pull, and the pull's requests reach a second listener of that proxy: a loopback port of its own (MEDIATORE_EGRESS_PULL_PORT, default 18129) that serves the one registry as /<host>/v2/... and nothing else, for gateway-placed routes only, with no credential, no challenge answered and no redirect followed by the puller. No jail rule lists that port (the sandbox uid's firewall set names the proxy's port and the claim's destinations; Landlock admits the proxy's port alone), and root's puller reaches it because the host table admits the loopback interface; the guest refuses a pull port that is the proxy's or a destination's. The proxy sends each request in origin form to a gateway's inject port with Host the registry's. Every other claim keeps today's order (the pull as root, then the proxy) and rel-guest-agent-registry unchanged.

ADR-0043 decision 2: for a registry that is a placed audience (audiences[]: via delegated, credential basic, inject gateway, the registry as the one egress entry, rules admitting only the registry API's read paths) the inject Envoy originates TLS to the registry's host and the authorizer's answer adds Authorization: Basic, the person's own user name and secret opened from the claim's sealed envelope. No registry token is created and no credential, the secret or anything derived from it, reaches the pool VM; the Bearer a registry would mint can live hours (measured: 9000 seconds), which is why the gateway places Basic itself (the operator's Artifactory accepts Basic on /v2/, measured 2026-11-15). The datacenter firewall must let the gateways reach the registry (an external control).

ADR-0045 decisions 4, 6 and 7: the sandbox API appends each accepted batch to the claim's Secret ring (LogStore::append_logs, KubeStore in crates/mediatore-claims; the memory ring under dev_mode), rolling to a new 64 KiB segment when the open one is full and deleting the oldest beyond logs.max_bytes; the user API reads it back (read_logs) for the owner; the leader's resync sweeps the segments of claims that ended logs.retention_secs ago or whose record is gone (sweep_logs), and the audit sweep of a sandbox deletes its segments with its session Secrets. At most two writes a second per printing claim (the batch limit); a write conflict between the two replicas is retried on resourceVersion.

Decided, not built (ADR-0049): node attestation of a guest with no vTPM (the banlieue firecracker provider class) by the x509pop attestor instead of the TPM one. The in-guest agent proves possession of the private key of a certificate its host signed for the guest's own key (EC P-256, the key never leaves the guest) and that chains to a CA in the per-host bundle; the agent ID is spiffe://<td>/spire/agent/x509pop/<issuer CN>/<subject CN>. The agent re-attests at about half its SVID lifetime and does not outlive its certificate (fail closed). Same transport as rel-spire-agent-server; keeps rel-spire-agent-server for every guest with a vTPM.

Decided, not built (ADR-0049): the SPIRE server reads the per-host CA bundle as the x509pop attestor's static trust anchor; a leaf signed by a CA outside the bundle is refused, and a server-side call per guest is never made.

Decided, not built (ADR-0049, ADR-0006 unchanged): for a guest attested by x509pop the watcher declares the node entry (mediatore-node-<...>) as a ClusterStaticEntry whose parent is spiffe://<td>/spire/agent/x509pop/<issuer CN>/<subject CN>, selected by an explicit attestation method (tpm or x509pop), never guessed from the data present. The issuer CN is the host's CA name the administrator asserts on the Provider (spec.attestation.hostCa) and the subject CN is the machine's UID published on its status (attestationSubject), both control-plane facts available before the guest boots; both are validated against the path-segment alphabet before any request. Same RBAC and admission policy as rel-watcher-entries; no admin SVID, no token minting.

flows.name: Claim a sandbox and act as the user
flows.description: The happy path from login to a delegated downstream call: login, claim, bind, subject fetch, jail, token.

transitions.description: User logs in; receives a token with aud = mediatore.
POST /v1/claims; mediatore validates the token and derives the subject.
mediatore creates an AgentSandbox with spec.subject; its reconciler creates the owned VirtualMachineClaim and the store record keyed by the claim's UID (ADR-0008).
banlieue binds a Ready, already-attested pool member and mirrors its EK certificate onto the claim.
The watcher hashes the EK certificate's public key, resolves the node, and declares the claim's ClusterStaticEntry (admission policy checks the shape).
The controller manager renders the entry over the private socket and reports status.set; the watcher marks the claim live.

The in-guest agent fetches the subject, the workload, the egress endpoints and the pull credential for the image's registry, if any (ADR-0022), over its node SVID, creates the sb- user and mounts the per-claim sandbox tmpfs (ADR-0021).

The guest pulls the workload image into the tmpfs as the rootfs, manifest and layers verified against their digests and the manifest digest logged (ADR-0021); then it loads the nftables ruleset keyed by the sb- uid (ADR-0020), starts the egress proxy as that user with the claim's routes and a fresh phantom token (ADR-0025), and starts the jail in the VM's network namespace.
The workload calls http://127.0.0.1:3128/<host>/<path> with the phantom token; the proxy checks the host against the claim's routes and the method and path against the audience's rules.
The proxy presents its claim SVID over mTLS and trades it for a short-lived, audience-scoped token, kept in its memory only.
The proxy forwards the request to the downstream API with the real token in place of the phantom, on the user's behalf.

flows.name: Release and cut-off
flows.description: Any of four independent cut-offs stops the sandbox acting as the user; this is the ordered normal release.

transitions.description: DELETE /v1/claims (or the TTL fires). The record (status.record on the AgentSandbox, ADR-0034) is revoked: /v1/token refuses immediately.
The ClusterStaticEntry is deleted; the controller manager removes the server entry and the workload's SVID stops within the agent sync interval.
The VirtualMachineClaim is deleted (or its deletion observed).
banlieue destroys the member, vTPM included; the guest agent tears down the jail and user regardless.

flows.name: Node bootstrap: from EK certificate to node SVID
flows.description: How a fresh pool member gets the in-guest agent's identity without the broker ever listing agents or holding a SPIRE admin credential (ADR-0006, ADR-0007).

transitions.description: banlieue publishes the member's vTPM EK certificate on VirtualMachine.status (banlieue ADR-0045) before GuestReady.
